The *Bhadditthivimānavatthu* (Vv 22), translated as "Lovely Lady’s Mansion", is a verse text belonging to the *Vimānavatthu* collection of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. In this discourse, the Supreme Buddha questions a female deity concerning the karmic cause through which she acquired a rare tree standing beside her heavenly mansion [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records five translations of the work across five languages [SuttaCentral].
SuttaCentral records thematic and textual associations between the *Bhadditthivimānavatthu* and numerous canonical texts, including several other *Vimānavatthu* discourses (Vv 15, Vv 19, Vv 23, Vv 24, Vv 25, Vv 37, Vv 52), the *Nimijātaka* (Ja 541), the *Surucijātaka* (Ja 489), the *Revatīpetavatthu* (Pv 39), the *Mittātherīgāthā* (Thig 2.7), and suttas from the Aṅguttara and Saṃyutta Nikāyas (AN 3.37, AN 3.38, SN 10.5) [SuttaCentral].

The largest internal matches occur with its commentary, the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* (matching segments §4.1–11.3), as well as the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* and the *Nimijātaka* (Ja 541, sharing segments §5.1–7.3) [DharmaNexus]. Extensive formulaic passages (notably §4.1–9.3) are shared with neighboring celestial mansion texts, including the *Niddāvimānavatthu* (Vv 25), *Lakhumāvimānavatthu* (Vv 19), *Visālakkhivimānavatthu* (Vv 37), *Uposathāvimānavatthu* (Vv 24), and *Soṇadinnāvimānavatthu* (Vv 23) [DharmaNexus].
